package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects Smith & Wesson's deployed version at time of attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is a malicious JavaScript skimmer designed to steal customer payment data by intercepting and exfiltrating sensitive information entered on the checkout page. This is a classic example of Magecart-style attacks, where attackers exploit web platform vulnerabilities to inject code that harvests credit card and personal data.

execution_context.trigger: When a user submits the checkout or payment form during a session on the website
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the Magento website's checkout page, either as an inline <script> or within a loaded JavaScript file associated with the checkout process
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form fields
Ability to intercept form submission events
Network access to send HTTP/HTTPS requests to external domains

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user submits the checkout form, the code intercepts the form submission event, collects all form data including payment details, and sends this data via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled external domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive customer payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment form submissions and exfiltrates the entire form data to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is a definitive sign of a web skimming attack and is never legitimate on a payment page.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors or the merchant's own backend, never to unrecognized or unapproved third-party domains. Intercepting and sending full form data externally is a direct violation of PCI DSS and standard security practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may send non-sensitive analytics or event data to third-party services, or transmit payment data to authorized payment gateways, but never full payment details or PII to unknown or untrusted domains.
key_indicators: JavaScript event listeners attached to form submissions on checkout or payment pages
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from the checkout page to domains not owned or operated by the merchant
Use of FormData or similar APIs to capture all form fields, including sensitive data
Presence of obfuscated, minified, or dynamically injected scripts in critical payment workflows
References to external script sources or endpoints that are not part of the legitimate payment infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Magento platform to gain unauthorized write access to the website's codebase.
Malicious JavaScript skimmer is injected into the checkout page or a JavaScript file loaded during the checkout process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in customer browsers

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits the checkout form, the skimmer intercepts the form data and sends it to the attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to checkout or payment form submissions
Outbound HTTP or HTTPS requests from checkout or payment pages to domains not on the merchant's allowlist
Presence of obfuscated, minified, or dynamically injected scripts on sensitive pages, especially those handling payment data
Use of FormData or similar APIs to capture and transmit all form fields from payment forms
file_indicators: Unexpected or unauthorized changes to JavaScript files associated with the checkout or payment process
Inline <script> tags with event listeners on payment forms that were not present in the original codebase
References to external scripts or endpoints from non-whitelisted or unrecognized domains within checkout page source code
network_indicators: POST requests from client browsers on checkout pages to domains or IP addresses not associated with the merchant or payment processor
Unusual or anomalous outbound traffic patterns from checkout or payment pages to unknown external domains, especially during form submission events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and audit JavaScript assets on checkout and payment pages for unauthorized modifications, especially scripts that hook into form submissions and transmit data externally. Enforce a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict allowed script sources and destinations for form data. Analyze network traffic from customer browsers for suspicious outbound POST requests during checkout. Regularly compare deployed web assets against known-good baselines to detect unexpected or obfuscated scripts, and investigate any references to non-whitelisted domains.
